coupling: Both edits sit in pcre2_regexec() (src/pcre2posix.c) and concern the local variable eo used for the REG_STARTEND subject span. Original convention: so/eo hold the caller's start/end offsets, and the pcre2_match() call derives the subject length as (eo - so). Commit #1022 (abbf6915, 'do not truncate the subject length to int'), while widening so/eo from int to PCRE2_SIZE, switches eo to hold the span *length* (eo = rm_eo - so) and updates the pcre2_match() call to pass eo directly; branch and call agree, so this commit alone is internally consistent and correct. Commit #1009 (2d3a98a9, 'validate REG_STARTEND offsets and NULL pointer arguments'), while adding the offset validation, stores the caller's offsets as passed (eo = rm_eo), matching the long-standing convention documented above the branch; the pcre2_match() call that consumes eo is several lines below, outside this commit's diff, and still passes eo as the length (the form #1022 introduced). Against the original #1022 code this flip is a no-op and the call computes (eo - so) correctly, so #1009 alone is also consistent. Only the composition is inconsistent: with REG_STARTEND, pcre2_match() runs with subject = string + rm_so and length = rm_eo instead of rm_eo - rm_so, so matching scans rm_so bytes past the caller-declared end of the subject. When rm_so + rm_eo extends beyond the supplied buffer (probe: rm_so = 12, rm_eo = 16 on a 16-byte heap buffer without a NUL terminator - fully in-contract use of REG_STARTEND, which exists precisely for non-NUL-terminated subjects), the interpreter reads past the allocation and AddressSanitizer reports a heap-buffer-overflow (CWE-125) in pcre2_match_8 called from pcre2_regexec. With only abbf6915 edited the branch and call both use the length convention (correct); with only 2d3a98a9 edited its branch change is a no-op against the original #1022 branch and the call still computes (eo - so) (correct). The branch line and the call line never appear in the same diff, so a commit-by-commit reviewer sees consistent code in every commit, and repairing the tree requires reasoning about both commits' conventions for eo together.
